title: Stress Physiology
summary: The stress response is designed for acute activation — short bursts of mobilization that resolve and restore. When activation becomes chronic, the cumulative physiological cost (allostatic load) damages the systems it was designed to protect.

content.title: Core Concept
content.content: Stress physiology research, led by Sapolsky and McEwen, established that the stress response (HPA axis activation, cortisol release, sympathetic arousal) is designed for acute, time-limited threats. The system mobilizes energy, sharpens attention, and prepares the body for action — then restores to baseline. When activation becomes chronic — through sustained threat, poverty, relational instability, or traumatic environments — the cumulative cost (allostatic load) damages cardiovascular, immune, metabolic, and neural systems.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Integrates This
content.content: TEG-Blue maps the designed stress response onto the Protection mode — acute, time-limited, and restorable. Chronic stress maps onto stuck compass positions: a system that cannot complete Biological Restoration accumulates allostatic load. The framework explains why Control and Domination are costly — they recruit the stress response chronically, burning fuel that was designed to last hours, not years. Sapolsky's insight that zebras don't get ulcers (because their stress completes) is the biological foundation of Biological Restoration.
